The district includes:



The Palakkad Gap.

Fertile plains.

River valleys.

Forests.

Hills.

Mountain ranges.

123.2 Climate



Palakkad has a tropical monsoon climate, but its weather differs from many other Kerala districts because of the Palakkad Gap.



The gap allows dry continental winds from Tamil Nadu to enter the district, resulting in:



Hotter summers.

Lower humidity than many coastal districts.

Good air circulation.

Seasonal variation in rainfall.

123.3 Seasons

Summer

March to May.

Hot and comparatively dry.

Temperatures often higher than in most parts of Kerala.

Southwest Monsoon

June to September.

Moderate to heavy rainfall, especially in the Western Ghats.

Northeast Monsoon

October to November.

Additional rainfall, mainly in eastern areas.

Winter

December to February.

Pleasant weather with cooler nights.

123.4 Temperature



Average temperatures generally range between:



Summer: approximately 25°C–38°C

Winter: approximately 20°C–32°C



Palakkad often records some of Kerala's highest daytime temperatures during summer.



123.5 Rainfall



Rainfall varies considerably across the district.



Western Ghats receive heavy rainfall.

Plains receive moderate rainfall.

Eastern rain-shadow regions receive comparatively less rainfall.



Rainwater supports:



Agriculture.

Forest ecosystems.

Reservoirs.

Groundwater recharge.

123.6 Palakkad Gap



The Palakkad Gap is approximately 30–40 km wide and is one of the most important natural mountain passes in the Western Ghats.



Its significance includes:



Influencing Kerala's climate.

Facilitating trade and transportation.

Allowing movement of plants and animals.

Connecting ecosystems of Kerala and Tamil Nadu.

Introduction



Malappuram is one of Kerala's most geographically diverse districts, extending from the Arabian Sea on the west to the Nilgiri foothills and the Western Ghats in the east. The district includes sandy beaches, estuaries, rivers, wetlands, forests, hills, plantations, and fertile agricultural plains.



It is especially known for the Bharathapuzha (Nila) River, the historic Nilambur forests, and the internationally important Kadalundi Bird Sanctuary. These ecosystems support a rich variety of wildlife, agriculture, fisheries, and eco-tourism.

Introduction



Wayanad is Kerala's only district situated entirely on the Western Ghats plateau. Renowned for its cool climate, mist-covered mountains, dense forests, rivers, waterfalls, wildlife sanctuaries, and fertile valleys, it is one of India's richest ecological regions.



The district forms part of the Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve, a UNESCO-recognized biosphere reserve that spans Kerala, Karnataka, and Tamil Nadu. Its forests provide vital wildlife corridors linking protected areas across South India and support an extraordinary variety of endemic plants and animals.

Wayanad experiences a tropical highland monsoon climate.



Its characteristics include:



Pleasant temperatures throughout most of the year.

Cool mornings and evenings.

Heavy monsoon rainfall.

Frequent mist in higher elevations.

Lower temperatures than Kerala's coastal districts.



Its elevation, generally between 700 and 2,100 metres above sea level, strongly influences its climate.

June to September.

Heavy rainfall nourishes forests, rivers, and plantations.

Moderate rainfall that benefits agriculture.

Winter

December to February.

Cool and often misty, especially in higher elevations.

Winter: approximately 12°C–25°C

Southwest Monsoon

June to September.

Heavy rainfall nourishes forests, rivers, reservoirs, and agricultural lands.

Northeast Monsoon

October to November.

Moderate rainfall supports agriculture.

Winter

December to February.

Pleasant and comparatively dry.

Wayanad, located in the northern Western Ghats of Kerala, is one of the state's most famous hill tourism destinations. The district is known for its mountains, forests, wildlife, waterfalls, caves, plantations, tribal heritage, and scenic landscapes.
